# European shares join global sell-off as AI fears mount

Richard Connor | Srinivas Mazumdaru with AFP, Reuters

November 6, 2026

European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets. [...] US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

0816 GMT – Shares of European semiconductor companies are in decline after investors dumped Asian stocks linked to artificial intelligence. South Korea’s SK Hynix closed 10% lower, while Samsung Electronics shed 7.4%. In Japan, chip-making equipment maker Tokyo Electron lost 7.2%. In Europe, shares of Dutch semiconductor-equipment maker ASML Holding and smaller rival ASM International are down 1.8% and 2.3%, respectively.
